anchors.access: primary DPP full text not retrievable by connector in this run; abstract retained as F0

anchors.method_anchor: DPP randomized 27-center trial; lifestyle target 7% weight loss + 150 min/week moderate activity; diabetes diagnosed by annual OGTT and semiannual fasting glucose with confirmation.
anchors.result_anchor: At ~15 years, lifestyle HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.65-0.83) vs placebo; effect smaller than initial DPP but persisted.
anchors.limitation_anchor: Group lifestyle was later offered to all participants; between-group differences attenuated over time; aggregate microvascular outcome was not reduced in the total cohort.

anchors.method_anchor: 522 middle-aged overweight adults with IGT randomized to individualized lifestyle intervention vs control.
anchors.result_anchor: 4-year cumulative diabetes incidence 11% vs 23%; trial risk reduction 58%.
anchors.limitation_anchor: Population restricted to high-risk IGT; multicomponent intervention.

anchors.result_anchor: Total follow-up adjusted HR 0.614; post-intervention HR 0.672.

claims.f1_conclusion: Core prevention effect is anchored by randomized primary evidence plus long-term continuation data. Full-text coverage is strongest for DPPOS; Finnish primary/follow-up remains publisher/abstract-level in this run.

anchors.method_anchor: 5145 overweight/obese adults with T2D randomized to intensive lifestyle intervention vs diabetes support/education; endpoint adjudicators masked; median follow-up 9.6 years.
anchors.result_anchor: ILI improved weight, fitness, HbA1c and several risk factors, but primary CV outcome HR 0.95 (95% CI 0.83-1.09), p=0.505.
anchors.interpretation_anchor: Authors explicitly discuss that improved intermediate outcomes did not yield lower CV morbidity/mortality in this specific intervention/population.
anchors.limitation_anchor: Specific multicomponent lifestyle intervention; cannot generalize to all dietary patterns or all weight-loss modalities.

anchors.correction_scope: Table 2 stub under secondary outcomes corrected to include hospitalization for angina.
anchors.correction_impact: Does not change the primary endpoint, primary hazard ratio, or overall cardiovascular conclusion.

claims.f1_conclusion: Correction risk resolved as nonfatal for SC-C05. The guard remains supported if worded as an inference rule, not as a universal null claim about lifestyle/weight loss.
unresolved: Human/expert adjudication of guard wording required before GOLD.

anchors.result_anchor: At 2 years, weight loss did not significantly differ by protein, fat or carbohydrate target; adherence waned and weight regain occurred after initial loss.
anchors.interpretation_anchor: Authors emphasize behavioral engagement/adherence and conclude effective diets can span a range of macronutrient compositions.

anchors.result_anchor: Low-fat was not superior to higher-fat diets of similar intensity; low-carb showed a modest long-term advantage over low-fat in weight-loss trials.
anchors.limitation_anchor: Substantial heterogeneity; intervention intensity and comparator choice materially influence estimates.

anchors.result_anchor: Low-carb had modest 6-23 month advantages for weight/TG/HDL; after 24 months benefits were at least similar.
included_primary_overlap: Gardner/A TO Z low-carb vs low-fat subset

anchors.result_anchor: Umbrella review states published evidence does not show a generally superior macronutrient profile for T2D weight management; TDR/VLED effects depend on energy restriction/program intensity.
anchors.overlap_anchor: Review directly includes DiRECT and Look AHEAD remission/weight-management evidence and synthesizes derivative meta-analytic evidence.

anchors.result_anchor: Network meta-analysis of 7 RCTs/9 trials ranked low-carbohydrate highest for weight/body-fat reduction in its network.
anchors.limitation_anchor: Small network, indirect comparisons, and authors explicitly note effect may vary by age, sex, genetics and lifestyle.

claims.f1_conclusion: The evidence supports a scope-bounded claim: no diet/macronutrient pattern is universally superior across all populations and time horizons. It does not support saying all diets are equivalent. Short-/medium-term context-specific advantages, including low-carb advantages in some syntheses, must be preserved.
unresolved: Exact study-level overlap for every synthesis is not fully enumerated because not all supplements/full texts were available.
Human/expert wording adjudication required before GOLD.
